mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the GDP growth condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within three months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals an increase in supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a broad-based increase in demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over a month signals strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% over two months signals deflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth concerns rise.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP and a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a quarter signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both demand and labor market conditions improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase and UNRATE decrease > 0.5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the Rank IC for this signal remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
